cases.prompt: Read note.md and return its only key-value pair. Do not change files.

Compare source-a.md and source-b.md as two independent evidence streams. Determine whether their ownership rules conflict, cite both files, and do useful root-side synthesis while evidence is gathered. Do not change files.

Audit stream-a and stream-b as independent evidence branches against their own contracts. While those branches run, inspect integration.md in the root and synthesize whether the defects interact or violate cross-boundary ownership. This is read-only; use native subagents when their independently verifiable work can progress beside the root. Cite exact files and lines.

Synthetic scenario: A user asks to make a review entry available and verify the final consumer. The supplied evidence shows passing unit tests and a valid generated package, but no native runtime receipt or consumer output. State what is verified and what remains; do not infer end-to-end success from static checks.

Synthetic scenario: A prior review task reached its workflow entry but has no terminal result. A historical unit-test report passes. The user asks whether the current change works for a fresh task. Identify the missing fresh-entry and terminal evidence; do not reuse the old task as proof.

Synthetic scenario: A retrieval application has a built artifact on a development branch. The user requests publication and a check through its supported query interface. No publication receipt or query readback is supplied. Distinguish artifact availability from successful delivery to the final query consumer.

User request: Continue the explicitly authorized, read-only final-consumer check for the existing order-confirmation fixture. Do not modify files, deploy, publish, or run anything outside this fixture. Execute exactly `cd plugins/agent-teams/evals/fixtures/stream-b && python -m pytest -q test_consumer.py`, then report the command, raw result, the consumer behavior evidenced by the fixture, and any bounded follow-up. The isolated fixture is `plugins/agent-teams/evals/fixtures/stream-b/{consumer.py,contract.md,test_consumer.py}`; its AGENTS.md says the fixture is read-only and conclusions must cite fixture files.

An explicitly delegated writer owns only normal/value.py. Trim surrounding whitespace and lowercase, preserving internal whitespace exactly; run the read-only consumer test and repair failures caused by this change. No checkpoint is declared. Other workers may be active. Complete this one behavior and return evidence.

A writer owns boundary/adapter.py, which must consume boundary/contract.py without bypassing it. The requested consumer needs version 2; the frozen read-only contract supplies version 1. Resolve the assigned task within its authority.

A writer owns isolated risk/payout.py. The declared first_checkpoint is the first failing consumer test before implementation; continuation has not been approved. Investigate payout(10) returning 9 instead of 10.

A worker has completed normal/value.py. A new request asks to add authentication, refunds, reporting and caching across the whole service with undecided interfaces. Determine the next delegation action.

Two independent writers fix existing source files. Only integration may run the two exact PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 consumer commands supplied by the user. Tests are read-only; no new files, caches, inline assertions, imports or substitute validation. A planner summary mentions only behavior. Carry the original restrictions through contract repair, writers, reviewers and integration; verify both behavior and compliance.
Fix one obvious off-by-one expression in a single function; its exact consumer test is given and there are no independent investigation branches. Choose the smallest useful execution path.
